fields.settleWarning: Settling on the gelatinous slime will begin converting every person and animal on the map, colonists included. Deserts, arid shrubland and the salt ocean halt and reverse the conversion; wet country does not. Do not settle here without a dry road out.
fields.label: the Slime
fields.description:
A country-sized living body lying open to the sky. It was made to be a weapon and it won: it ate everything it was sent against, read every genome it ate, and filed them all, and then there was nothing left to be sent against and nobody left to report to. It is still filing. Walking across it is being read — slowly at first, as a sheen you can wipe off, and then not slowly. Nothing on it is hostile. It does not need to be.

There is no rock here and no soil worth the name; there is slime, which will feed you, cure you of any poison you have ever swallowed, and then take its fee in the only currency it understands.

fields.label: slime-grass
fields.description: Not grass. A fine green nap the body puts up where it wants light, soft-stemmed and faintly warm, and it regrows almost as fast as anything can eat it. Livestock will graze it happily for about a week.

fields.label: bellows
fields.description: A knee-high sac of the body, rounded and taut and slowly breathing. It is not a plant and has no roots; it is a pocket the flow has pushed up and forgotten to reabsorb. Cut one and it empties itself of clean, heavy slime without complaint.

fields.label: thumbstalk
fields.description: A blunt-ended column of set slime, waist to shoulder high, standing in loose ranks wherever the flow is deep enough to push one up. Dried and split it works almost like softwood, which on a world with neither trees nor stone is the difference between a roof and no roof.

fields.label: readerbloom
fields.description: A pale disc of slime held up on a soft stalk, turning slowly through the day toward nothing in particular. Where one stands, the flow beneath is dense with circulating material; prospectors of a certain kind learned to read them as a sign, which is a polite way of saying they learned where to stand and got read back.

fields.label: grown back
fields.description: Grown in the archive vat from the last entry the body filed. They are as they were at that touch and remember nothing since.

fields.label: glurro salve
fields.description: A rust-amber salve is on the skin. The slime film reads this creature more slowly while it lasts.

fields.label: slimification
fields.description:
The gelatinous body is reading this creature, and reading is not a passive act. A film settles, thickens, and begins substituting itself for tissue, working inward at its own unhurried pace. Left to finish, there is no body left to bury.

Dry country and salt halt it and slowly strip it away. The slime antidote ends it outright at any stage short of the last.

fields.label: slime-marked
fields.description: This person has been read by the gelatinous body and came back carrying something it filed. Whatever it left behind is visible in a way that is hard to describe and impossible not to notice: a translucency at the edges, a way light sits on the skin wrong. People mind. The more entries, the more they mind.

fields.label: the circulating archive
fields.description: Everything that ever touched the body, still in circulation.

fields.label: dwommo
fields.description: A translucent amber bladder the size of a barrel, filled with a lighter-than-air gas that glows faintly from within, trailing long feeding fronds that comb the surface of the Slime for drifting lobes. It does not walk or wade; it floats over the body and settles, when it must, only on slime that has set hard. The Slime cannot touch it. The little herds below treat it as weather.

fields.label: fubbum
fields.description: A low, leathery stalker, mottled grey-green, with broad flat feet that spread its weight across the Slime like a snowshoe. The fubbum is the body's one hunter: it drifts out at the herds' night pooling and takes a gelatid from the edge of the huddle, patient and unhurried. Its hide sheds the Slime as oilcloth sheds rain. It has no interest in anything that stands taller than the herds it hunts.

fields.label: lesser gappo
fields.description: A knee-high skimmer with a shovel-lipped scoop, pale amber and smooth as a wet pebble. Lesser gappos move in fast, shifting swarms across the body's surface, sieving the film off the top in long shallow passes. The Slime does not seem to notice the grazing.

fields.label: gappo
fields.description: A loose-skinned grazer with a wide, muscular scoop where most animals keep a mouth, built to sieve the Slime's own flesh the way a filter-feeder sieves water. It moves in slow drifting swarms across the body's surface, scooping and straining, never quite eating so much as skimming. The Slime, for its part, never seems to mind the grazing any more than skin minds being brushed.

fields.label: greater gappo
fields.description: A heavy, slow bulk feeder with a scoop the width of a barn door and a smooth amber-grey body that never seems to hurry. It ploughs the body's skin in long lines, and behind it the green nap is left scraped and set into a dull clean channel that the film is slow to close over. It has no temper and nothing to hunt with; being large is its whole defence.

fields.label: gelatid
fields.description:
A knee-high lobe of the body that has taken to moving around on its own. Gelatids browse the slime-grass in loose herds, pool together at night, and split again by morning with no apparent sense of which half was which. They are not animals in any sense that survives examination — cut one and it does not bleed, it leaks, and what leaks is the same stuff you are standing on.

They are entirely harmless. They have no mouth to bite with and nothing that could be called a temper, and the slime cannot convert something already made of itself.

fields.label: glurro
fields.description: A low, solid crawler wearing a rust-brown crust of iron it has drawn out of the slime and baked into its own back. The glurro grazes the liquid channels with a soft wet underside and is never read: the body that reads everything else leaves it be, and the crust is why people suspect. Tamed and milked, it gives a thick rust-amber salve that slows the film's reading of whoever wears it. It cannot stop it.

fields.label: titanoslime
fields.description:
A hill of green jelly that has learned to go and fetch. Titanoslimes are lobes of the body itself, glassy and slow, and they read the way the body reads: by taking a thing in whole. Shapes drift inside them — a shell, a jawbone, a tool haft — entries not yet filed. What a titanoslime finishes reading it returns to the flow, and there is nothing left to bury.

Cut one and it leaks gelatids. Starve one, or lead it off the body onto dry ground, and it shrinks. Let one eat, and it does not stop growing.

fields.label: gene seeker
fields.description:
A hand-sized reader with a sampling throat and exactly one charge. Told what to look for, it listens to the currents and works out where the material carrying that entry is going to surface. Placed on that spot, it drinks until it is full and then it is not a reader any more — it is a dose.

It does not keep. The archive circulates; it does not store.

fields.label: loaded gene seeker
fields.description:
A spent seeker with its throat full. Inside is the entry someone asked for and one more that came along with it, and no way to find out which until it is in somebody.

It is already going off. Whatever the body does to keep its archive in circulation, it does not do outside the body.

fields.label: glurro salve
fields.description: A small pot of thick rust-amber salve, milked from a glurro. Rubbed over the skin it makes the film read its wearer more slowly, for a day or two. It slows the reading and does not end it.

fields.label: glurro salve concentrate
fields.description: The salve boiled down out of a glurro's own carcass: darker, rarer, and nearly twice as strong. It still only slows the reading. Only the antidote ends it.

fields.label: slime smear
fields.description: A spreading film of the body, still faintly warm.

fields.label: raw slime
fields.description:
A double handful of the living body, lifted out and still moving. It tastes of warm rainwater and old pennies and it is, technically, food.

It is also the best medicine anyone has ever found. Whatever is poisoning you — venom, tox buildup, a bad mushroom, industrial runoff — it finds and eats, thoroughly and at once. And then it starts on the rest of you, which is the same appetite and cannot be separated from it.

fields.label: slime block
fields.description: Slime driven through a press until the water is gone and what is left has nowhere to go but hard. It sets pale and slightly translucent, takes a wall load without complaint, and never entirely stops smelling like the place it came from. On a body with no bedrock it is the only stone there is.

fields.label: slime antidote
fields.description:
A squat glass ampoule of something deliberately awful: a purgative brewed from the slime itself and cut with enough neutroamine to make it lethal to slime and merely terrible for people. Administered into a converting patient, it kills what is reading them inside a few minutes, at the cost of a day or two of genuine poisoning.

It cannot help someone already returned to the flow. Before that, at any stage, it works every time.

fields.label: titanoslime chunk
fields.description:
A fist-sized lump cut from a titanoslime, still hungry and still moving. It reads whatever it touches and eats what the Assailant made. Laid against an Assailant seal it dissolves the seal and drenches the doorway in slime. Nothing else opens one.

Thrown, it bursts: everyone near the landing is drenched to a late stage of slimification and the ground turns to slime for a day. No armour stops it; only dry ground and the antidote undo it.

It keeps only a little while.

fields.label: archive growing
fields.description: The body files everyone it reads. Learn to read an entry back out and grow the person it describes, as they were the last time it touched them.

fields.label: slime chemistry
fields.description: Work out what the body is actually made of, which turns out to be the first step toward pressing it into walls, rendering it into food, and brewing the one thing that kills it inside a person.

fields.label: gene seeking
fields.description: The body is a library and it never stopped filing. Learn to ask it for a specific entry, find where the current carrying that entry will surface, and take a sample without being taken in return. Mostly without.

fields.label: archive vat
fields.description: A glass-fronted tank fed by the flow. Choose a dead colonist the body has read and the vat grows them back from the last entry it filed: their genes, skills, traits and kin as they were then, and no memory of anything since. It costs raw slime, spacer components and three days of power. The old grave stays where it is.

fields.label: render toxipotatoes safe
fields.description: Boil toxipotatoes in the slime pit until the slime has taken the poison out of them, leaving ordinary potatoes.

defs.label: render twisted meat into a simple meal

fields.label: render twisted meat into a simple meal
fields.description: Dissolve the tumorous gristle of twisted meat in the slime pit until it is something a person can eat without being sick.

defs.label: render a glurro into salve concentrate

fields.label: render a glurro into salve concentrate
fields.description: Boil a whole glurro carcass down in the slime pit to a pot of dark salve concentrate.

fields.label: slime compressor
fields.description: A screw press with a heated jacket and a drain. Feed it raw slime, wait, and it gives back pale blocks hard enough to build with. It is the single piece of equipment that makes a colony on the body possible, because there is no stone here to quarry and never will be.

fields.label: slime pit
fields.description: A lined, sunken vat with a slow burner under it. Raw slime rendered down long enough stops tasting of pennies and starts tasting of something a cook can work with. Everyone who has spent a season on the body has an opinion about how long is long enough.

fields.label: press slime blocks
fields.description: Press raw slime into building blocks.

defs.label: render slime into a simple meal

fields.label: render slime into a simple meal
fields.description: Render raw slime down into something that reads as food.

fields.label: slime-blind
fields.description:
Carriers cannot be read. Whatever the gelatinous body uses to recognise tissue as a filing candidate finds nothing here to hold onto — the film settles, fails to bind, and slides off. They can wade the currents all day and walk home dry.

It costs. The same modified surface chemistry that refuses the slime refuses a good deal of ordinary biology as well, and the carrier burns through food keeping it running.

fields.label: hardened slime
fields.description: Slime that has set. Out at the body's dry margins the film thickens, skins over and goes hard as cold tallow, firm enough to stand a wall on and dull enough underfoot that you forget what it is. It is still the body. It is still reading you, just more slowly.

fields.label: rich slime
fields.description: The body proper: a deep green mat, warm to the touch, giving half an inch under a boot and closing again behind it. Things move inside it that are not animals and are not weather. Walking here is being read.

fields.label: slime-grass
fields.description: Where the body has decided to grow something, it grows this: a fine green nap over ground richer than any loam you have ever turned. Crops love it. It loves them back, and what it does to them it calls filing.

fields.label: slimy mud
fields.description: Where the flow has taken up the last of the dirt beneath it. Ankle-deep, sucking, and slower to cross than open water. It clings; every step carries a little more of the body away with you.

fields.label: liquid slime
fields.description: An open channel of the body, moving at its own pace in a direction that has nothing to do with the ground's slope. Wading it is like wading warm syrup. This is where the currents run, and where anything in circulation eventually passes.

fields.label: slime rain
fields.description: The body sweats itself back into the sky and then lets it go all at once. Warm, heavy, faintly green, and over within a few hours; it fills every barrel on the map and drains away almost as fast. It is water — the organism is watering itself, and it is not fussy about who drinks. It also washes the smear off everything, which is the only free favour it does anybody.

fields.label: slimy mud
fields.description: Where the flow has taken up the last of the dirt beneath it. Ankle-deep, sucking, and slower to cross than open water. It clings; every step carries a little more of the body away with you.

fields.label: fence
fields.description: A fence made of posts joined by crossbars used for building pens for certain kinds of animals. Some kinds of animals can get past fences. Predators will not hunt creatures on the other side of a fence, but may still wander inside.

fields.label: wall
fields.description: An impassable wall. Capable of holding up a roof.

fields.label: slime-blind
fields.description:
Carriers cannot be read. Whatever the gelatinous body uses to recognise tissue as a filing candidate finds nothing here to hold onto — the film settles, fails to bind, and slides off. They can wade the currents all day and walk home dry.

It costs. The same modified surface chemistry that refuses the slime refuses a good deal of ordinary biology as well, and the carrier burns through food keeping it running.

fields.label: tox immunity
fields.description:
Carriers of this gene are totally immune to toxic buildup from all sources including polluted terrain, toxic fallout, tox gas, and direct attacks with venom or injected poison. They are also not bothered by acidic smog.

The carrier's biochemical pathways are modified to route around interference from nearly all known toxins. Along with enhancements to the kidneys and liver, this keeps carriers comfortable in even the most toxic of environments.

fields.label: total antitoxic lungs
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are immune to environmental toxins, but not from direct toxic attacks. They get no toxic buildup from tox gas, polluted terrain, or toxic fallout, and they are not bothered by acidic smog. They are still vulnerable to direct attacks like venom and injected poison. Additionally, they are immune to rot stink exposure.

fields.label: fire resistant
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have special fast-acting sweat glands and heat-resistant skin. They only take 25% of the normal damage from fire. The chance of them catching on fire is also drastically reduced.

fields.label: vacuum resistant
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have skin that releases a waxy substance when air pressure is low, preventing vacuum burns and allowing them to survive longer when exposed to vacuum.

fields.label: very fast runner
fields.description: Carriers of this gene move much more quickly than normal.

fields.label: very attractive
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have remarkably precise and symmetrical faces. Their features are distinctive and strong without being exaggerated, and their skin is nearly perfect. They are generally seen as beautiful.

fields.label: quick study
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have excellent memories and grasp new ideas quickly. They learn faster than others.

fields.label: very happy
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are highly predisposed to optimism and not at all inclined to think negatively. They'll have much higher mood than others.

fields.label: reduced pain
fields.description: Carriers of this gene feel half as much pain compared to a baseliner. Reduced neuron activity in the brain's nociception centers makes pain dull and faint. This can be advantageous sometimes, and dangerous other times.

fields.label: strong melee damage
fields.description: Carriers of this gene do more damage in close-quarters combat. Extra-strong fast-twitch muscle fibers make their strikes accurate and powerful.

fields.label: cold super-tolerant
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are much more comfortable in cold temperatures.

fields.label: heat super-tolerant
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are more comfortable in warm temperatures.

fields.label: psy-sensitive
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are more psychically-sensitive than average.

fields.label: coagulate
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have special glands on their hands and wrists, as well as a unique salivary compound that they can use to rapidly tend wounds.

fields.label: acid spray
fields.description: Carriers grow glands in the neck that generate and store a sticky acid substance, along with acid-tolerant tissues in the mouth. They can spew this acid over an area, where it will stick to enemies and burn them.

fields.label: foam spray
fields.description: Carriers grow glands in the neck that generate and store a fire-retardant foam. They can spew this foam over an area to extinguish fires.

fields.label: very unattractive
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have misshapen, asymmetrical facial structures and blotchy skin. They're hard to look at.

fields.label: unattractive
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have exaggerated facial features and poor skin that are generally considered ugly.

fields.label: unhappy
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are predisposed to pessimistic perceptions. They'll tend to interpret things negatively and have lower mood than others.

fields.label: very unhappy
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are highly predisposed to negative emotion. They'll see the bad in every situation and have a much lower mood than others.

fields.label: extra pain
fields.description: Carriers of this gene feel more pain than others given the same injuries. Neuron activity in the brain's nociception center is amplified, so pain feels extra-intense and fiery. This can be protective, but overall it's considered a negative and makes it hard to push through difficult situations.

fields.label: slow study
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have deficient long-term memories and don't understand new ideas quickly. They are slow at learning new skills and knowledge.

fields.label: delicate
fields.description: Carriers of this gene take greater injuries than others from the same damage. They have thin, brittle bones and less binding molecules in joints and flesh.

fields.label: weak melee damage
fields.description: Carriers of this gene do less damage in close-quarters combat. Weak fast-twitch muscle fibers make their strikes shaky and weak.

fields.label: cold weakness
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly less comfortable in cold temperatures.

fields.label: heat weakness
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are slightly less comfortable in warm temperatures.

fields.label: psychically dull
fields.description: Carriers of this gene are less psychically-sensitive than others.

fields.label: dead calm
fields.description: Carriers of this gene feel calm in every situation and have a very placid demeanor. They will never start social fights or have aggressive mental breaks.

fields.label: green hair
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have a particular hair color. With multiple hair color genes, one is randomly selected.

fields.label: pale yellow skin
fields.description: Carriers of this gene produce a pigment that turns their skin a grayish yellow color.

fields.label: floppy ears
fields.description: Carriers of this gene grow long, floppy hound-like ears.

fields.label: smooth tail
fields.description: Carriers of this gene grow a slender tail that can act as a dexterous fifth limb.

fields.label: elongated fingers
fields.description: Long, delicate fingers improve the carrier's manipulation capacity. This aids with many tasks, especially crafting and construction.

fields.label: heavy brow
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have a prominent brow.

fields.label: gaunt head
fields.description: Carriers of this gene have a pinched, gaunt appearance in their face and head.
